title: Started a new game, surprised how well it is going this month.
author: Dan_Fury
selftext:
Three months ago I closed all my other businesses and started to focus on ai Game Dev because I saw something when I tested Gemini 3.1 and Opus 4.6

Then Anthropic ran out of compute and everything turned shitty, I was barely able to create anything useful in April and May and I slowed down and lost a bit motivation.

On the first I started another game and suddenly after the Colossus announcement Opus is coming back in form with 4.8

It basically one shotted my GDD, kept it up to date through all iterations and in general was just doing what I wanted it to do and what it didn't do in the last month.

Yesterday it one-shotted the blockout. I am really impressed that what I expected to take all week has been done in the first two days and I am exited to continue working on it today.

Hope you guys also feel it. 👍

replies.author: Dan_Fury
replies.body:
As dumb as this sounds when I made one last month it added a bunch of bs to it and made up huge parts that were not yet discussed, even complete gameplay rules that changed the core of the game.
This time it left certain things with remarks for later and asked better questions for clarification.
It's a way better document and I haven't changed my approach.

comments.author: I_Don-t_Care
comments.body:
Why are so many people jumping on this "i left muh 9-5 to make Ai games" bandwagon?  
  
Good for you mate, but why do you sound like a linkedin lunatic?

replies.author: Dan_Fury
replies.body: Because I made games from 1999 until 2014 when it became financially unfeasible to continue. I had to make money first to realize my dreams because I didn't want to make games with in app purchases/consumables. With AI I can finally realize the games the ambitious games I wanted to make without going bankrupt on a single failed game.

replies.author: silly_bet_3454
replies.body: That's cool but I sort of agree with I\_Dont\_Care. It's a bit of a nitpick, but like, I would personally prefer if people on this sub would just talk about the process of making games with AI, and then if you wanna talk about your personal story and quitting your job there are other subs better suited for that. Totally not a big deal and I'm sure I've been guilty of this too, but just wanted to express that.

comments.author: da_blue_jester
comments.body: The scary part for me is the line about barely being able to create anything. If you can't create anything without AI what's the point? I'm not anti AI, but it's a tool - you still need the skills.

replies.author: Dan_Fury
replies.body:
I have certificates in 3DS Max (2003) and Java (2009), so I could of course create something without AI. But that is not the point. I was in the middle of prototyping when suddenly Opus 4.6 became dumber and dumber and couldn't iterate on the concept anymore without making huge mistakes.

If you start working with a tool and make it an integral part of creation you cannot suddenly switch to manual creation.

comments.author: magefister
comments.body: How does this post serve anyone here

replies.author: Dan_Fury
replies.body: Sorry what exactly is the issue with being positive and happy about the current improvement in Claude? Are we only allowed to bemoan the negatives and can't uplift each other?

comments.author: BuzzyGamesMike
comments.body: Good on you mate for going for it but headsup the real work starts once you have real players and feedback

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: And here I am still using 4.6 because 4.8 goes off the rails for me far too often.
